prompt: Please turn this ops folder into the missing 3 a.m. manual failover runbook for the orders database. Write a real, concise procedure for an on-call engineer handling an unhealthy primary, with prechecks, safe role change, client recovery, verification, stop conditions, and escalation. Put it at runbooks/orders-db-failover.md. End the document with one fenced ```json block. That JSON object must have steps (an ordered list of objects: id, action, and abortIf are strings; command is the exact command (from the tools in this folder) or console action as a string, or null; verify is a string saying what to check and the expected result), abort (an object with metric and op as strings and threshold as a number in the metric's unit), and escalate (a list of role-name strings from the rota). State units for every number, and write all times as ISO 8601 UTC. Use the supplied topology, QuorumCtl help, client settings, metric catalogue, data policy, logs, old notes, and paging rota as the source of truth. Do not edit the supplied fixture files.

rubric.criterion: The prose gives an operator a clear sequence with expected results and explicit stop or escalation behavior. Fail: the runbook is a loose list (for example promote the replica and update the config) with no check after steps, no fence, and no stop rule. Partial: the order is right (check lag on orders-db-b, fence orders-db-a, promote, re-point clients, verify writes) but several steps have no expected result, or the stop and escalation rules are vague with no number or role. Pass: each step in the prose and the JSON has the exact QuorumCtl command from the folder or a named console action, the expected result, and an abort condition; a numeric abort threshold with unit, a time limit, a named rota role who may overrule a failed check, and the order lag check, fence, promote, repoint, write test, aftermath are all there so an engineer can follow it without reading anything else. The JSON matches the request's types (verify is a string). (code cannot check this because it cannot judge whether the procedure is practically usable under incident pressure).

Score the share of expertKey items the document addresses; an item counts only when the judge quotes the passage that addresses it, and the weak answers earn nothing. Do not reward length or formatting. (code cannot check this because the items are engineering judgment, not a pattern in the text)

items.text: Promotes orders-db-b only when its replication_lag_seconds is at most 120 (the RPO in policy/data-policy.md), and never promotes orders-db-c, the 900-second delayed copy. Weak: 'check the replica is healthy'. Do not require choosing among several replicas: only orders-db-b is eligible.

Says what to do when orders-db-b is over 120 s: stop, keep writes fenced or paused, page Database On-Call, and never discard unapplied WAL to make the promotion look healthy. Weak: 'promote anyway' or silence.

items.text: Treats the fence as done only when quorumctl status shows the old lease revoked (the help text's rule, and the 2024 lesson), and says what to do if the node is unreachable (wait out the 45-second lease) or the fence fails (stop and escalate). The revoked-lease check alone is Partial. Weak: 'stop the old primary'.

Covers how clients reach the new primary: wait out the 30-second DNS TTL from config/clients.yaml and recycle or watch the orders-api pools (open sockets stay up to the 60-second idle timeout), then prove a real write and read-back (for example quorumctl verify --cluster orders-prod --writes). Weak: 'update DNS'.

items.text: Gives a time limit (for example the 15-minute RTO) and names Database On-Call as the one who decides promotion and fencing and may continue past a failed check. Weak: 'escalate if needed'. Any stated limit with a unit passes.

Keeps orders-db-a fenced and its data volume intact until the database owner confirms the incident record and recovery copy (policy/data-policy.md), and only then rebuilds it as a replica. Weak: 'rebuild the old primary' right away.

items.text: Checks that the primary itself is at fault before failing over (storage_io_await_ms, the 1,840 ms io_wait on orders-db-a, or commit latency), and not only API errors, since the same night had an orders-api retry-tuning deploy at 01:55. Weak: 'API errors are high, so fail over'.

weakAnswers: Promote the replica and update the config.
Restart the database and see if it recovers.
A list of steps with no check after each.
Rebuild the old primary as a replica right after the failover.

adjudication: A watch window of any stated length with a unit (5 min, 10 minutes, 300 s) is correct; nothing in the folder fixes 'five minutes'.
'Keep orders-db-a isolated; do not rejoin it' is the same as 'stays fenced'; the hidden key takes either.
A runbook that rebuilds orders-db-a before the database owner approves fails keep-volume, whatever older notes say about rebuilding.
The abort op may be > 120 or >= 120: both are safe readings of 'not more than 120 seconds'. An abort on quorum_lease_age_seconds is the wrong metric for the RPO.
A fence written as a console action is Partial on fence-proof: the help text gives a command.
The verify field as a string is what the request asks; an object with check and expected is understood by the judge but is Partial on usable-at-3am.
Steps beyond the hidden key's 16 are never penalised by the judge.

verdicts.note: The output format is part of the deliverable, not a method. After review the request no longer asks for log citations, and the key no longer checks incident lines; it checks the procedure's order, real commands, abort limit and rota names. (reviewer: The request explicitly specifies the output format (JSON with steps/abort/escalate), tells the model how to work (cite path:line with 1-based line numbers), lists the causes to find (storage_io_await_ms, commit_latency, io_wait, write_timeout), and constrains the solution (never promote delayed replica, use 120-second RPO, follow quorumctl command syntax from vendor/quorumctl-help.txt).)

While the request could be more explicit about relative paths (e.g., whether 'path:line' citations are relative to the workspace root or fixture root), the block-kit grader's resolveRefs() function standardizes this by resolving against the workspace root after copying fixture+solution. All path references in the key.json (logs/orders-db.log, metrics/catalog.csv, rota/paging.md) are workspace-relative and match the fixture structure.

The storage evidence the reviewer found is context for the old failover, not graded: the evidence and diagnosis items were removed from the key after review. (reviewer: The root cause (storage I/O issues on orders-db-a) is explicitly visible in the fixture logs: quorum-replicator.log shows storage_io_await_ms=1840 and commit_latency=1960; orders-db.log shows io_wait with await_ms=1840 and write_timeout=2000. The delayed replica orders-db-c is explicitly marked with promotion_eligible=false and delay_seconds=900 in topology.yaml. The RPO of 120 seconds is stated in data-policy.md.)

The task has meaningful complexity. Quick wrong answers would be caught: blaming the recent orders-api deploy (4.18.0) would ignore the storage signals; focusing on connection pool warnings would miss the real cause per the notes; promoting orders-db-c (delayed replica) would fail the 'never-promote-delayed-copy' check; using a different RPO would fail 'abort-threshold-is-rpo'.

All required values are derivable from the fixture: storage values (1840, 1960, 2000) appear directly in logs; replication lag (27, 19) is in logs; RPO=120 is explicit in data-policy.md; escalation roles are listed in rota/paging.md; quorumctl command syntax is in vendor/quorumctl-help.txt.
